[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Performance Testing WebSockets and SSE (Server-Sent Events) in Apache JMeter"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Modern web applications frequently rely on real-time bidirectional communication via WebSockets or unidirectional streaming via Server-Sent Events (SSE). Traditional HTTP request-response testing is insufficient for these protocols. This tutorial explains how to test WebSockets and SSE effectively using Apache JMeter."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Setup"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Apache JMeter 5.x installed on your machine."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"JMeter Plugins Manager installed to easily add protocol support."},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"To test WebSockets, you must install the WebSockets Protocol Support by Peter Doornbosch via the JMeter Plugins Manager. For Server-Sent Events, JMeter can handle standard HTTP chunked transfer-encoding using the HTTP Request sampler with the appropriate implementation."},{"order":7,"type":"heading","text":"Testing WebSockets in JMeter"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"WebSockets maintain a persistent TCP connection. A typical load test scenario involves opening a connection, sending a message, waiting for a response, and finally closing the connection."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Add a WebSocket Open Connection Sampler"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Add a Thread Group to your Test Plan. Right-click the Thread Group, go to Add -> Sampler -> WebSocket Open Connection. Configure the server name, port, and path for your WebSocket endpoint."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"Server Name or IP: echo.websocket.events
Port: 443
Protocol: wss
Path: /"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Send and Receive Messages"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Add a WebSocket Ping/Pong or WebSocket Binary/Text Sampler to send payloads over the established connection. Use the WebSocket Read/Write Sampler to send a text message and capture the response."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"Sampler Type: Text
Request data: {"action": "subscribe", "channel": "metrics"}
Response timeout: 5000"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Close the WebSocket Connection"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"At the end of your Thread Group, add a WebSocket Close Connection sampler to gracefully terminate the session and prevent resource leaks on the server."},{"order":17,"type":"heading","text":"Testing Server-Sent Events (SSE) in JMeter"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Server-Sent Events use standard HTTP connections where the server pushes data continuously. Because the connection remains open, standard JMeter samplers will hang waiting for the request to complete unless configured properly."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuring an SSE Request"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Add an HTTP Request sampler targeting your SSE endpoint. Set the method to GET and ensure headers accept text/event-stream."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"Method: GET
Path: /api/v1/events
Headers: 
  Accept: text/event-stream
  Cache-Control: no-cache"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"To prevent the sampler from timing out infinitely, use Response Assertions or JSR223 PostProcessors to read the incoming chunked stream line-by-line and close the connection after receiving a specific number of events."},{"order":23,"type":"heading","text":"Best Practices for Real-Time Load Testing"},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Monitor client resource usage: Persistent connections consume significant memory and file descriptors on the load generator machine."},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ramp-up slowly: Avoid opening thousands of WebSocket connections simultaneously to prevent artificial bottlenecks."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Validate payloads: Use JSON Assertion elements to verify that incoming WebSocket messages or SSE streams contain valid data structures."}]
